Questions.answer: The outer cover is damaged and the plug feels loose.
options: It does not supply power to the equipment.
The outer cover is damaged and the plug feels loose.

Questions.answer: Because they do not want to delay their assigned tasks.

Questions.question: Why does someone still use the faulty power socket during busy periods?
Questions.answer: Because there are not enough free sockets nearby.
options: Because it works better than the other sockets.
Because there are not enough free sockets nearby.
Because there are more than enough free sockets nearby.

Questions.question: What action does the instructor decide to take at the end of the dialogue?
Questions.answer: He arranges repairs and replacement of the cable and socket.
options: He asks trainees to be more careful with the equipment.
He plans to check the area himself later in the week.
He arranges repairs and replacement of the cable and socket.

activity_c.text: Good morning.
Before we start today’s practical session, is everything okay in your area?
I know that you always check the setup early in the morning, so I just wanted to ask you a few questions before everyone begins work.
Good morning, sir.
Actually, I wanted to mention two things.
I don’t usually complain, and I try to manage small problems on my own, but I think this should be reported.
There are some issues with the extension cable and the power socket near the shared work table.
Okay, thanks for telling me.
What exactly is the problem with the extension cable?
The cable still works, but the outer cover is damaged and worn out in several places.
We use it every day, and people frequently pull it across the floor instead of lifting it properly.
The plug sometimes feels loose as well, but we rarely notice it until someone points it out during work.
Right, that doesn’t sound safe at all.
Loose connections can easily cause accidents.
And what about the power socket near the table?
The socket sometimes sparks slightly when we plug equipment in.
It doesn’t happen all the time, but it happens often enough to be a concern.
We usually try to avoid using that socket, especially when sensitive equipment is involved.
But during busy periods someone always ends up using it because there aren’t enough free sockets nearby.
Do you normally report issues like this straight away, or do you usually try to work around them and carry on?
To be honest, we usually work around them.
We rarely stop work to report small faults because we don’t want to delay the tasks assigned to us in the morning.
We often assume the maintenance team will notice it later during inspections.
I’m glad you reported it now.
Small problems often become serious if we ignore them for too long.
I’ll arrange repairs today and ask maintenance to replace both the cable and the socket.
As we say, a stitch in time saves nine.
